title: Project Configuration
description: Contract for non-secret Terraform project configuration.
$comment: Cloud-specific values live only in the clouds map. Everything under vms refers to them by abstract label, so moving a VM to another provider is a one-word change. Cross-references between the two - a size label existing in the target cloud's machine_sizes, default_cloud naming a declared cloud, every cloud in use owning a bastion - are outside what JSON Schema can express and are enforced by variable validation inside the per-cloud Terraform modules.

default_cloud.$comment: Cloud hosting every VM that does not override it. Must be a key of clouds; Terraform checks that.

common_labels.$comment: Applied to every resource. Terraform adds application, environment, managed_by, role and cloud on its own - do not repeat them here.

bastion.$comment: Core infrastructure, not a workload. One block for the whole project: a bastion is created on every cloud that hosts a workload, and its size, image, disk and address are derived from that cloud's profile.

network.$comment: Provider-independent networking. Subnet ranges are per-cloud and live in clouds.<name>.subnets.

ui_public_ports.$comment: Traefik terminates TLS on 443 and solves the ACME challenge with TLS-ALPN-01, so nothing ever listens on 80. Opening it would expose a port with no service behind it.

observability.$comment: Provider-independent alerting settings. Thresholds and log retention have defaults in the Terraform modules; only the recipient has to be written down.

alert_email.$comment: Where every alert and budget notification goes. AWS sends a subscription confirmation to this address first.

thresholds.$comment: Overrides for the alert thresholds. Every key is optional and falls back to the module default.

clouds.$comment: One profile per supported provider. A profile translates the abstract labels used under vms into that provider's own identifiers.

allOf.$comment: A GCP network has no CIDR of its own; its subnets carry the ranges.
GCP names a principal as type:identifier.
AWS resources are addressed by region and credentials, never by a project identifier.
An AWS budget is scoped to the account behind the credentials, so there is nothing to name.
AWS names a principal by ARN.

vms.$comment: Application workloads only. Every one lives on default_cloud unless it sets cloud; the bastion each cloud needs is derived from the top-level bastion block, not listed here.

resource_label.$comment: Key into one of a cloud profile's lookup maps. Never a provider-specific identifier.

zone.$comment: GCP places instances here; AWS also binds its subnets to it, since an AWS subnet cannot span availability zones.

network_cidr.$comment: AWS only. An AWS VPC carries its own range and every subnet must fall inside it; a GCP network has no range of its own.

machine_sizes.$comment: Abstract size label to this provider's machine type, for example tiny to e2-micro or t3.micro.

disk_types.$comment: Abstract disk label to this provider's volume type, for example balanced to pd-balanced or gp3.

images.$comment: Abstract image label to this provider's image reference. An AWS AMI ID is region-scoped, so it belongs to this profile and not to a shared list.

secret_version_managers.$comment: Identities allowed to add a new version to every secret this cloud holds. Adding a version never grants reading one. The field is named the same on both providers because the difference is only in how each names a principal, and each cloud's branch under clouds checks its own format.

budget_usd.$comment: Monthly spend on this cloud, in US dollars, above which the billing alert fires. Absent means no budget is created.

billing_account.$comment: GCP only. A budget belongs to a billing account, not to a project, so the project alone is not enough to create one.

ssh_port.$comment: Port Ansible moves the SSH daemon to. Until it does, a fresh bastion listens on 22.

allowed_cidrs.$comment: Source ranges permitted to reach the bastion. Never 0.0.0.0/0 - that defeats the point of having one.

size.$comment: Defaults to tiny. A bastion forwards connections and nothing else.

type.$comment: Label resolved through the hosting cloud's disk_types map.

ssh_users.$comment: Maps Linux usernames to public SSH keys. Private keys and local key-file paths are not accepted.

secret_mappings.$comment: Maps application environment variable names to non-secret secret-store IDs.

cloud.$comment: Overrides default_cloud for this VM only. Omit to follow the default.

size.$comment: Label resolved through the hosting cloud's machine_sizes map.

image.$comment: Label resolved through the hosting cloud's images map.

internal_ip.$comment: Must sit inside the hosting cloud's matching subnet. AWS reserves the first four addresses and the last address of every subnet.
